title: Bosch Colors Across Brand Guide and Bosch Digital Design System
intent: Structured extraction of long-form research on how Bosch colors are defined, governed, tokenized, and applied across the Bosch Brand Guide and the Bosch Digital Design System (BDDS).
recommended_audiences: product teams producing Bosch-compliant digital outputs

covered_topics: Relationship between Bosch Brand Guide and BDDS
Brand colors, base colors, accent colors, signal colors, emphasis colors, exception colors
Digital Color System and Digital Color System 2
Design token naming and usage logic
Light mode and dark mode behavior
Interaction states such as default, hovered, pressed, disabled, focus
Color flow across Brand Guide, Frontify, Figma Bosch UI Kit, FROK, Digital Color Picker, and token repositories
Accessibility, WCAG alignment, and legal framing
Governance, compliance, updates, and migration logic
AI usage rules for Bosch-compliant color generation
excluded_topics: Confidential implementation details beyond high-level system logic
scope.research_style: Long-form synthesis translated into normalized JSON for AI consumption

executive_summary.core_conclusion: Bosch color governance is centralized in the Bosch Brand Guide and operationalized for digital products through BDDS. The Brand Guide defines the authoritative color identity, usage principles, and accessibility expectations. BDDS converts those principles into a token-based digital color system consumed by Figma libraries, FROK, and related tooling.
executive_summary.authority_model: The Bosch Brand Guide remains the upstream source of truth for color decisions. BDDS is the digital extension and implementation layer, not a competing visual language.
practical_reading: Use Bosch Brand Guide and BDDS documentation as the canonical reference layer for colors.
In digital products, prefer color schemes, tokens, and official components instead of direct HEX or RGB values.
Digital Color System 2 makes Bosch color usage more modular, accessible, tokenized, and implementation-ready.
Accessibility is embedded into the system through approved pairings, contrast-aware schemes, and predefined component states.
AI-generated Bosch UI or visual outputs should use semantic color roles and token language rather than arbitrary color descriptions.

Digital extension that translates Bosch Brand Guide principles into digital design foundations, UI components, token systems, implementation logic, and accessibility-ready interface patterns.

governance_rules: Treat Bosch Brand Guide plus BDDS as the root authority for Bosch-compliant color usage.
Use official color schemes and design tokens instead of arbitrary direct HEX or RGB values in digital applications.
Use official Bosch UI Kit and FROK-compatible component logic whenever possible.
Custom color divergence should be treated as an exception requiring justification.
Teams should maintain update and migration discipline when BDDS color libraries or tokens change.
Accessibility and contrast requirements are part of color governance, not optional post-processing.

expected_team_behavior: Monitor Brand Guide and BDDS updates.
Update Figma libraries when official Bosch UI Kit updates are released.
Update FROK or token package versions when implementation libraries change.
Avoid freezing old token versions when accessibility or contrast updates have been released.
Validate non-standard color usage against official guidance before implementation.

brand_guide_color_model.definition: The Bosch Brand Guide defines Bosch color identity, color categories, usage intent, and accessibility rules across touchpoints. It supplies the upstream corporate color logic that BDDS translates into digital systems.

color_categories.primary_intent: Corporate identity and brand recognition, especially symbol/logotype and selected brand-defining elements.
color_categories.digital_usage_interpretation: Reserved and controlled. Not the default clickable color in ordinary UI because red can conflict semantically with error or critical status patterns.
color_categories.ai_rule: Do not overuse Bosch Red as a decorative or UI accent color. Reserve Bosch Red for brand-defining or explicitly approved exception cases.

color_categories.primary_intent: Backgrounds, surfaces, text, containers, dividers, and general visual structure.
color_categories.digital_usage_interpretation: Maps into base schemes and plain schemes for fills, fronts, borders, surfaces, and neutral interface hierarchy.
color_categories.ai_rule: Use neutral base colors as the default foundation for Bosch UI. Prefer white or light neutral backgrounds for standard light-mode outputs unless a dark theme is explicitly requested.

color_categories.primary_intent: Selective emphasis, clickable elements, calls to action, and controlled visual hierarchy.
color_categories.digital_usage_interpretation: Maps into BDDS accent schemes with major, minor, pure, and nested types plus interaction states.
color_categories.ai_rule: Use accent colors sparingly and functionally. Do not make color the predominant stylistic device.

color_categories.primary_intent: Error, warning, success, neutral, note, and status communication.
color_categories.digital_usage_interpretation: Maps into signal schemes such as error, neutral, note, success, and warning.
color_categories.ai_rule: Use signal colors only for their semantic status purpose. Do not use warning or error colors as decorative accents.

color_categories.primary_intent: Support diagrams, reporting, illustrations, information graphics, and tonal hierarchy.
color_categories.digital_usage_interpretation: Maps into tokenized shade systems and front/fill pairings. Higher brightness gradations can support light backgrounds; darker gradations support text and contrast.
color_categories.ai_rule: Use gradations only in relationship to their base or accent family, not as arbitrary standalone palette choices.

color_categories.primary_intent: Support bright default Bosch design and dark theme alternatives for screen contexts.
color_categories.digital_usage_interpretation: Maps into light mode and dark mode token resolution, including front/fill changes and adjusted contrast pairings.
color_categories.ai_rule: Default to light mode unless dark mode is explicitly requested or contextually necessary. In dark mode, rely on semantic tokens rather than manually inverted colors.

usage_principles: Bosch design is bright and predominantly white in standard use.
Color is used selectively and functionally rather than as the dominant stylistic device.
Accent colors should support hierarchy, interaction, or meaning.
Color gradations can support diagrams, reports, and illustrations, but should remain connected to the approved color family.
Color combinations must support readability and accessibility.

bdds_color_model.definition: BDDS operationalizes Bosch Brand Guide colors for digital products using semantic schemes, components, tokenized values, state logic, and accessibility-aware pairings.

digital_color_system.role: Digital color foundation for Bosch interfaces.
digital_color_system.core_function: Converts brand color guidance into reusable digital roles and implementation-ready tokens.
important_characteristics: Consistent use across design and code
Support for light and dark modes
State-aware behavior for default, hovered, pressed, and disabled states
Support for theming, multibranding, and future headless architecture

digital_color_system_2.summary: Digital Color System 2 is a major evolution of Bosch digital color handling. It introduced centralized design tokens, modular naming, streamlined schemes, unified type attributes, consistent disabled states, optimized palettes, and broader theming readiness.
changes_and_features: Full multibrand capability with individual brand color configurations on request
Modular structure optimized for naming and attributes
Streamlined and more intuitive color scheme names
Unified type attributes to ensure consistent color usage
Removal or replacement of redundant schemes
Optimized palettes including black and white by default
Availability of color definitions as tokens through a dedicated token repository
Future expansion toward foundational tokens, interface formats, and themes
digital_color_system_2.strategic_interpretation: Digital Color System 2 is not only a palette revision. It is a move toward a portable, headless, token-driven design system that can be consumed by design tools, code libraries, and AI systems.

token_ontology.definition: A Bosch color token is a named semantic value that describes what a color is for, not only what numeric color value it has.

token_dimensions.meaning: High-level color role or category, such as base, accent, plain, integrated, error, neutral, note, success, warning, emphasis, or special.
Variant inside a scheme, such as major, minor, pure, or nested.
Interaction or availability state, such as enabled default, enabled hovered, enabled pressed, or disabled.
The UI part receiving the color, especially fill for backgrounds and front for text, icons, or foreground elements.
Resolved output for light mode or dark mode.

known_token_name_examples: emphasis green / major / enabled default fill
token_usage_rules: Use semantic token names rather than raw color values when describing or generating Bosch digital interfaces.
Use paired fill and front tokens to maintain accessible contrast.
Use state-specific tokens for hover, pressed, disabled, and focus states.
Use theme-aware tokens instead of manually converting light theme colors to dark theme colors.
Do not invent local token names unless creating a clearly marked prototype abstraction.
do_not_use: Decorative color gradients that are not defined by Bosch guidance
Status colors for non-status decorative purposes
Bosch Red as a generic UI action color without approval

color_scheme_mapping.digital_intent: Neutral structure, text, backgrounds, surfaces, dividers, and quiet UI foundations.
color_scheme_mapping.ai_prompt_instruction: Use Bosch-like neutral foundations, white or light-gray surfaces, high contrast typography, and minimal visual clutter.

color_scheme_mapping.digital_intent: Brand identity and recognition, not ordinary interactivity.
color_scheme_mapping.ai_prompt_instruction: Reserve Bosch Red for brand identity. Avoid using it as default button, link, chart, or error color unless context explicitly requires it.

color_scheme_mapping.digital_intent: Clickable elements, calls to action, selected items, and controlled emphasis.
color_scheme_mapping.ai_prompt_instruction: Use a restrained accent system for interactive hierarchy. Keep accents consistent across the screen.

color_scheme_mapping.bdds_scheme_or_token_area: signal schemes: error, neutral, note, success, warning
color_scheme_mapping.digital_intent: Semantic status communication and user feedback.
color_scheme_mapping.ai_prompt_instruction: Use signal colors only for meaningful status communication. Pair color with text or icon cues.

color_scheme_mapping.bdds_scheme_or_token_area: shade scales and tokenized front/fill pairs
color_scheme_mapping.digital_intent: Controlled tonal hierarchy for information graphics, data visualization, reporting, and illustrations.
color_scheme_mapping.ai_prompt_instruction: Use approved shade families and avoid standalone arbitrary shades. Keep data colors accessible and readable.

color_scheme_mapping.digital_intent: Maintain consistent brand and accessible contrast in both bright and dark UI contexts.
color_scheme_mapping.ai_prompt_instruction: Default to light theme. When dark theme is requested, use dark base backgrounds and light foreground tokens rather than arbitrary inversion.

light_dark_theme_logic.default_behavior: Bosch digital design defaults to a bright, mostly white light theme unless dark mode is explicitly appropriate.

light_theme.foreground: Dark neutral or dark blue-toned text and icons
light_theme.accent_behavior: Accent colors are used selectively for clickable or high-priority interface elements.
light_theme.risk: Too many accent colors can create visual clutter and reduce hierarchy.

dark_theme.dominant_background: Dark base colors or dark shades, often conceptually close to dark blue or dark neutral foundations
dark_theme.foreground: Lighter front colors to ensure contrast
dark_theme.accent_behavior: Accent colors may require lighter gradations than their light-mode equivalents to maintain sufficient contrast.
dark_theme.risk: Manual inversion can break brand and accessibility; semantic tokens should be used instead.

light_dark_theme_logic.token_rule: The same semantic token should resolve to different underlying color values depending on theme mode while preserving role, hierarchy, and contrast.

states.meaning: Normal enabled appearance for static or interactive elements.
Mouse-over or pointer-hover feedback, usually implemented through a controlled shade change.
Active click or activation feedback, usually implemented through a stronger or darker/lighter shade depending on theme.
Unavailable or inactive component state. Digital Color System 2 emphasizes consistent disabled states across schemes.
Keyboard or accessibility focus indicator that must remain highly visible and clearly separate from decoration.

interaction_state_logic.implementation_rule: Interaction states should be implemented by official tokens or component variants, not manual color overrides.

tools_and_platform_flow.flow_summary: Bosch colors move from brand definition to digital implementation through a structured toolchain: Brand Guide defines the rules, BDDS translates the rules into a digital system, tokens encode the colors, Figma exposes them to designers, FROK exposes them to developers, and the Color Picker helps explore valid combinations.

pipeline: Bosch Brand Guide defines brand and color rules.
BDDS translates those rules into digital foundations, schemes, components, and tokens.
Token repository encodes the color system for tools and code.
Figma UI Kit exposes the tokens to designers.
FROK exposes the tokens and component logic to developers.
Digital Color Picker supports exploration and validation.
Products inherit consistent Bosch color behavior when they use official libraries and tokens.

accessibility_and_legal_model.core_statement: Accessibility is a first-class color requirement in Bosch digital design. Color choices must support readable contrast, inclusive perception, machine readability, keyboard focus, and legal compliance.
standards_and_laws_referenced: WCAG as international digital accessibility standard
European Accessibility Act and its 2025 implications in Europe
Regional legal diversity requiring accessible digital touchpoints
accessibility_rules: Use approved color combinations that satisfy contrast expectations.
Do not rely on color alone to communicate status or meaning.
Pair signal colors with text, icons, or other non-color cues.
Use official focus tokens and focus styles for keyboard navigation.
Avoid low-contrast bright text on light backgrounds.
Avoid text embedded in images without alternatives.
Maintain sufficient contrast across all interactive states.
Avoid custom color overrides that bypass tested front/fill pairings.
accessibility_and_legal_model.practical_implication: Using official BDDS tokens and components is the safest way to remain aligned with Bosch accessibility and legal expectations. Custom colors increase brand, usability, and compliance risk.

minimum_rules: Treat Bosch Brand Guide and BDDS as the root color authority.
Prefer semantic color roles over raw color values.
Default to white or light neutral backgrounds for Bosch outputs unless the user explicitly requests dark mode.
Use neutral base colors for structure and readability.
Use accent colors for interactive or high-priority elements.
Use signal colors only for semantic status feedback.
Reserve Bosch Red for logo, brand anchor, or special approved cases.
Use design-token language when generating UI or implementation prompts.
Do not invent decorative palettes that break Bosch visual consistency.
Include accessibility constraints in prompts by default.
When generating UI, specify states such as default, hover, pressed, disabled, and focus.

prompt_ready_language.general_ui: Create a Bosch-compliant digital interface using BDDS color logic: white or light neutral background, restrained accent color for clickable elements, semantic status colors only for feedback, accessible front/fill contrast, and official-style interaction states for default, hover, pressed, disabled, and focus.
prompt_ready_language.dark_mode_ui: Create a Bosch-compliant dark theme using BDDS semantic color logic: dark base background, light foreground text, accessible accent pairings, semantic signal colors, and no manual color inversion or arbitrary HEX values.
prompt_ready_language.dashboard_or_chart: Use Bosch-compliant neutral UI foundations with approved emphasis colors for data visualization. Keep emphasis colors distinct, accessible, and secondary to readability. Do not use Bosch Red or warning colors as generic chart colors unless the data meaning requires it.
prompt_ready_language.audit_or_critique: Review the interface for Bosch color compliance: verify use of official semantic color roles, restrained accent use, readable contrast, correct signal-color semantics, focus visibility, disabled-state consistency, and absence of arbitrary HEX/RGB overrides.

anti_patterns: Using Bosch Red as the default CTA color.
Using yellow as decorative emphasis instead of warning-related usage.
Using multiple bright accent colors on the same screen without semantic reason.
Creating low-contrast colored text on light backgrounds.
Manual dark-mode inversion without token logic.
Using screenshots or text-in-image as the only source of critical information.
Using color alone to indicate status.

brand_intent_to_digital_implementation.bdds_implementation: Reserved/special color role; not ordinary UI accent
brand_intent_to_digital_implementation.risk_if_misused: Confusion with error/status semantics and dilution of brand recognition

brand_intent_to_digital_implementation.brand_guide_expression: Base colors and bright white Bosch design
brand_intent_to_digital_implementation.bdds_implementation: base/plain/integrated schemes with front and fill tokens
accent major/minor/pure/nested tokens with state variants
brand_intent_to_digital_implementation.risk_if_misused: Users cannot distinguish interactive from non-interactive elements

brand_intent_to_digital_implementation.bdds_implementation: signal schemes: error, neutral, note, success, warning
brand_intent_to_digital_implementation.risk_if_misused: Incorrect severity perception or inaccessible status communication

brand_intent_to_digital_implementation.brand_guide_expression: Color gradations and approved accent families
brand_intent_to_digital_implementation.bdds_implementation: emphasis schemes and controlled shade systems
brand_intent_to_digital_implementation.risk_if_misused: Arbitrary colorfulness and loss of brand coherence

what_is_strongly_supported: BDDS is the digital extension of the Bosch Brand Guide.
BDDS is increasingly token-driven, especially through Digital Color System 2.
Digital Color System 2 affects Figma libraries and FROK.
Accessibility is embedded in Bosch color, typography, and component guidance.
Official tools and libraries should be preferred over custom local implementations.

Current migration status for a specific product team
Final legal conformance of a specific screen or product

For implementation, teams should consult the live Brand Guide, Digital Color Picker, token repository, Figma libraries, and FROK documentation.
